hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: Find a source form that changes WHICH of the two values is defined last before the call. Swapping the two defining statements was tried and REGRESSED (see probed_form), which is itself evidence that retail's defining order is the one we already have.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: yes - the dependence distance was read from the aligned raw view (`fnasm.py game/sys/ml_mem AllocFile 0x50:0x90 --raw --diff`), and both call-site values are confirmed to live in callee-saved r25/r29 in BOTH streams, so no register-assignment difference is involved.
hypothesis.statement: The exchange is the target scheduler hiding a one-cycle result latency, not a source difference. Retail computes `avail` at +0x68 (`subf r25,r7,r0`) and then issues the INDEPENDENT `addi r6,r29,0` at +0x6c before consuming r25 at +0x70; our stream issues `addi r5,r25,0` back-to-back with the subf. Any lever that reaches this is a scheduler lever, not a statement-order one.
